tagline: Just the board. Two tiny previews. One more perfect fit.
overview: Prism Fall is a focused Tetris-style game made with RedEngine's native 2D rules and renderer. The black-and-charcoal well fills the window edge to edge, without an outer frame, side gutters or cards. Only a slim header for score, hold and two tiny previews remains. Instructions live in the menus. Play Marathon for a high score, Sprint for a forty-line time, or Zen for steady-speed practice with a fresh well after a top-out. SRS wall kicks, a ghost piece, seven-bag randomization and responsive held movement make each placement deliberate.
story: There is no campaign to hurry through and no enemy to chase. You are tending a small well of coloured glass: every piece is another chance to turn an awkward space into a clean line. Marathon builds the pressure, Sprint makes every motion count, and Zen lets you return to the rhythm whenever the stack reaches the ceiling.
goal: Clear horizontal lines by filling all ten cells. Marathon ends when the well blocks a new piece or a piece locks above the visible board. Sprint ends successfully at forty lines. Zen refreshes the well after a top-out and keeps your score.
rules: All seven tetrominoes appear once per shuffled bag; the next two pieces are shown beside the well.
A full row disappears and every row above it shifts down. Clearing several rows at once earns more points.
Hold exchanges your piece with the reserve once per placement. A hard drop places and locks immediately; soft drop and hard drop earn distance points.
Rotations try SRS wall and floor kicks. A grounded piece has half a second before locking, with at most fifteen movement resets.
Combos, back-to-back four-line clears or T-spins, and perfect clears earn bonuses. T-spins use the three-corner rule; mini classification is not included.
Every ten cleared lines increases the Marathon or Sprint speed. Zen keeps a steady speed. Records are saved locally.

controls.action: D-pad/stick moves; up rotates; A drops/selects; X/B/RT holds; Start pauses

characters.name: The seven pieces
characters.description: I, O, T, S, Z, J and L each have their own colour. The hollow ghost shows where the active piece will land. A shuffled seven-bag gives you every shape before the next bag begins.

tips: Keep the surface level and avoid covering empty cells.
Use the small next previews before spending your hold.
Try Q to rotate the shorter way. Wall kicks can help a piece fit beside the edge or floor.
Pause whenever you need a moment. Zen is a forgiving place to practise.

gallery.caption: The opening placements: a large centred well, a ghost landing indicator and two small previews.
Nine lines cleared during the deterministic forty-piece showcase, using the same rules and renderer as the native game.
Thirteen lines and level two after forty actual placements; the score rewards clean stacking and consecutive clears.

why_made: The request was for a high quality Tetris game using the latest RedEngine, followed by publication and development feedback. The design focuses on dependable falling-block mechanics, reproducible engine tests and a minimal interface. The user specifically asked for less surrounding UI, a centred board and only one or two small next-piece hints; those constraints shaped the final layout.
prompt: Using the latest RedEngine, create a high quality Tetris game. Once complete, publish to RedEngineGames and add your development feedback to the engine for improvement
prompt_source: User request on 2026-10-21, followed by requests for a simpler UI, an edge-to-edge centred board, only one or two tiny next-piece previews, D-pad support and black/charcoal rather than navy.
